title: Entangled Schr\"odinger Bridge Matching
abstract: arXiv:2511.07406v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Simulating trajectories of multi-particle systems on complex energy landscapes is a central task in molecular dynamics (MD) and drug discovery, but remains challenging at scale due to computationally expensive and long simulations. Previous approaches leverage techniques such as flow or Schr\"odinger bridge matching to implicitly learn joint trajectories from data snapshots. However, many systems, including biomolecular systems and heterogeneous cell populations, undergo dynamic interactions that evolve over their trajectory and cannot be captured through static snapshots. To close this gap, we introduce Entangled Schr\"odinger Bridge Matching (EntangledSBM), a framework that learns the first- and second-order stochastic dynamics of interacting, multi-particle systems where the direction and magnitude of each particle's path depend dynamically on the paths of the other particles. translated_abstract: 在复杂能量景观上模拟多粒子系统的轨迹是分子动力学（MD）和药物发现中的核心任务，但由于计算代价高昂且模拟耗时较长，大规模应用仍然充满挑战。以往的方法利用流匹配或薛定谔桥匹配等技术，从数据快照中隐式地学习联合轨迹。然而，包括生物分子系统和异质性细胞种群在内的许多系统，会经历随轨迹演化的动态相互作用，这种相互作用无法通过静态快照捕捉。为弥合这一差距，我们提出了纠缠薛定谔桥匹配（EntangledSBM），这是一个学习相互作用多粒子系统一阶与二阶随机动力学的框架，其中每个粒子轨迹的方向和大小会动态依赖于其他粒子的轨迹。我们定义了纠缠薛定谔桥（Entangled Schrödinger Bridge，摘要在此处截断）……
tldr: 本文提出纠缠薛定谔桥匹配框架，首次建模多粒子系统中每个粒子轨迹随其他粒子轨迹动态耦合演化的随机动力学，突破了以往基于静态快照方法的局限，可应用于分子动力学模拟与药物发现。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces Entangled Schrödinger Bridge Matching (EntangledSBM), a framework that learns the dynamically coupled first- and second-order stochastic dynamics of interacting multi-particle systems—where each particle's trajectory depends on the paths of others—overcoming the limitations of static snapshot-based methods in molecular dynamics and drug discovery.
